summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a WebRTC-driven remote shell binary
details: The package tarball contains only package.json and a stripped ~12MB linux/arm64 Go binary at bin/sxt, with no README or source. Go build metadata for bin/sxt shows imports of github.com/pion/webrtc/v4 (with pion dtls/stun/turn/sctp/ice/srtp/datachannel), github.com/coder/websocket, github.com/creack/pty, and os/exec, plus DataChannel/OnMessage symbols and hardcoded "/bin/bash" and "/bin/sh" literals. This composition implements a WebRTC peer-shell agent: a remote peer, reached via a hardcoded WebSocket/TURN signaling endpoint and paired through a DataChannel, drives an interactive PTY-hosted shell on the machine running the binary, yielding full remote code execution on the installer's host. The published package name (sextant-cli-linux-arm64) is unrelated to the license field's source pointer at github.com/ddos798/claude_control, and no other documentation is shipped.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
